title: How Payment Infrastructure for South Asian Creators Works and How to Deploy It Today
author: COREMERCH
excerpt: Selling digital products from Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Pakistan, Bangladesh, or Zimbabwe is fully operational with sovereign commerce infrastructure that has no geographic restrictions.

content.text: In Pakistan and other South Asian countries, creators face significant barriers when trying to sell digital products online due to restrictions on platforms like Stripe and PayPal. This infrastructure gap leaves many without a reliable way to collect payments from international buyers. COREMERCH offers a solution, providing a sovereign digital commerce stack that enables creators to sell their products globally without relying on restricted platforms.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The COREMERCH infrastructure is built on a combination of free and paid tools, including GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, and NOWPayments, which provides automatic on-chain crypto payment verification. This approach allows creators to maintain full ownership and control over their data, eliminating the risk of platform restrictions or closures. By leveraging blockchain-based payments, creators can accept over 300 cryptocurrencies, including those with low fees like BSC, Solana, and TRON, making it easier to reach a global audience.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying the COREMERCH infrastructure, you'll need to have a clear understanding of your digital product offerings, including ebooks, courses, templates, and software. You'll also need to set up a GitHub account and familiarize yourself with Cloudflare Workers and NOWPayments. Additionally, you'll need to choose the right stack for your business, such as the Sovereign Starter Stack or the Edge Commerce Stack, depending on your specific needs and requirements.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Setting up your payment and delivery pipeline involves configuring your NOWPayments account, connecting it to your digital product store, and testing the payment processing workflow. You'll also need to set up your file delivery system, using services like Google Drive or Cloudflare R2, to ensure instant product delivery to your customers. This step is critical in ensuring a seamless and secure payment and delivery experience for your customers.
Sovereign digital commerce infrastructure gives you full ownership and control over your data.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once you've set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you're ready to go live and start processing transactions. This involves configuring your store's frontend, testing the payment workflow, and ensuring that your digital products are delivered instantly to customers. You'll also need to monitor your store's performance, track sales, and analyze customer behavior to optimize your business and improve the overall customer experience.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

The Edge Commerce Stack that COREMERCH deploys most frequently combines Cloudflare Pages for storefront hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend webhook handling and order processing, Supabase for order storage, Resend for transactional email delivery, and NOWPayments for crypto payment verification. The total monthly cost is zero. The scale ceiling is significantly higher than what most individual creators need — Cloudflare Workers handles 100,000 requests per day on the free tier, Supabase provides 500MB of PostgreSQL storage, and Resend delivers 3,000 emails per month. For a creator in any country on earth, this stack provides the same infrastructure as a well-funded e-commerce operation at no monthly cost, under their own accounts, with full data ownership from day one.
